newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria parlt approves 1,000 levs per mark peg.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria parlt approves 1,000 levs per mark peg.

text.p: Bulgaria's parliament on Wednesday approved a proposal pegging the lev to the mark as anchor in a currency board system, at an exchange rate of 1,000 per mark, parliament speaker Yordan Sokolov said.
"The proposal to peg the lev at 1,000 per mark has been approved by 134 votes," Sokolov said after the vote in the 240-seat parliament.
The cabinet-proposed lev/mark peg was included as an article in the new Bulgarian National Bank Law which is needed to make the currency board operational.
The law is being voted item by item and the parliament has yet to decide whether the fixed exchange rate will become effective immediately or on July 1, when the currency board is launched.
Under a $657 million reform and funding agreement with the International Monetary Fund, Bulgaria has pledged to introduce a currency board system to try to stabilise its crumbling economy.
The system requires levs in circulation to be exactly matched by central bank issue department foreign exchange reserves.
Bulgaria will enter the currency board arrangement with issue department reserves of around $1 billion, IMF team leader Anne McGuirk said on Tuesday. -- Sofia Newsroom, (+359-2) 911 88
